messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Dail and Madsen Models and Removal Design
parts:
Hi Roy,

Currently, unmarked does not include a function for fitting a Dail-Madsen-like model to removal sampling data. This is on my to-do list, but I'm not sure if I will ever have time to add it. I can definitely be done though, and one of the BUGS engines might be your best bet.

If you do some simulation studies, feel free to report back here, or post a link to a paper. And thanks for the kind words.

Richard


On Thu, Mar 21, 2013 at 12:46 PM, Roy Martin <royw...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Group,

Last summer we started a mark-recapture study on stream fishes across 9 streams with 3 levels of land use type. We started our sampling and marking last summer, using the depletion/removal electrofishing method common in stream fish studies. However, because we are a little concerned that one of the two species we marked may have issues with readability and mark-retention, we have considered dropping it from the study. Nevertheless, we would really like to get some basic demographic information on this species and would like to assess the possibility of employing the Dail and Madsen approach tor estimating omega and gamma for unmarked populations. My first question for the group is whether our depletion design can be accommodated by the Dail and Madsen model (even if not currently implemented in "unmarked"). I understand that the Chandler et al. implementation in unmarked accommodates this design, but we'd really like to get estimates of survival and recruitment.

Second, I have simulated a dataset with similar expected abundances for these fishes across the same number of sites and created a habitat covariate with the hypothesized effects. In the sampling simulation, given the removal design "issue", I instead simulated a typical, non-removal robust design sampling of the simulated populations (with expected p and M = 9, T = 4, J=3). After running pcountOpen on the simulated dataset, it appears that the D-M model works fairly well at estimating all of the parameters. However, I'm wondering if there might be additional information out there regarding the performance of the D-M model at different sizes of M and T (and J). Or if there are any additional simulations that might be helpful.

Thanks so much, in advance, for entertaining my questions and many kudos to the unmarked creators as well as to all of the folks involved in the original research. It is indeed an exciting paradigm to watch unfold.

Sincerely,


Roy Martin
Ecological Exposure Research Division
USEPA Office of Research and Development
Cincinnati, OH
